newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine tyre makers urge tariff cut delay.
newsitem.headline: Philippine tyre makers urge tariff cut delay.

text.p: Philippine tyre manufacturers asked the government on Thursday to defer the reduction of tariffs on imported new tyres.
Based on a timetable set by the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA), tariff on new tyres will be cut by five percentage points every year starting 1997 to only 15 percent by 1999.
The present levy on imported tyres is 30 percent.

The Tyre Manufacturers Association of the Philippines, in which Sime Darby Pilipinas Inc and Philtread Tyre and Rubber Corp are major members, said local manufacturers are already facing competition from cheap Indonesian and Chinese tyres.
ASEAN, the Association of South East Asian Nations, includes Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

"While the local tyre manufacturers could still operate under the current unfavourable market situation, they fear that additional pricing leeway accruing to tyre improters as a result of lower import duties ... would make their investments unviable," the association said in a letter to the Board of Investments.
The organisation said tyre companies have recently invested more than one billion pesos to upgrade their production facilities.
